groups.headline: Moog is the strongest long in the group: a 39.9% June-quarter beat, a raised FY guide, +23% backlog and the only meaningful FY1 revision move (+7.3% in 90 days). Leidos is the solid secondary — four straight beats, 8-up/0-down revisions and enhanced guidance, but slower growth. Woodward is the weakest: its beat size has decayed from 31.2% to 2.9% over four quarters, revisions are flat, and a premium multiple leaves no cushion for an in-line print.
groups.tactical: WWD prints first (Oct 29) — it is the short and also the group's read-through: a soft print pressures LDOS/MOG-A estimates into their Nov 1/3 prints, while a strong one argues for covering early. Establish the MOG-A long ahead of Nov 1 and keep LDOS as the lower-beta pair leg given its modest multiple cushions an in-line result.

Demand is broad — missile controls, space vehicles, commercial aircraft volume/pricing, data-center cooling pumps — so the beat is not single-program. The multiple is at theme median, so the print must deliver, but the filed operating detail says it can.

best_long.risk: Tariff-claim margin benefit does not repeat; if adjusted margin ex-claims steps down, the raised guide looks front-loaded and the stock gives back the post-Q3 move.

leaderboard.summary: The best risk/reward sits in names where filed guidance raises, broad upward revisions, and a fresh decisive beat all point the same way: SMCI, VRT, SEZL and FA lead the longs, while COIN, TRIP and RHI lead shorts whose estimate bases are actively collapsing into their prints. Note the overlap: MOG-A, VRT and SMCI all lean on the same AI/data-center capex driver, so they are one macro idea expressed three ways, not three independent bets. On the short side, WWD and EMR are the weakest cases because they fight mildly positive revision priors; COIN, TRIP, RHI, SHAK and GPN align with their own downward revision tape and are cleaner.
